service: Hyper3D Rodin (hyper3d.ai), Business plan, through the hyper3d MCP server
prompt: A fat cream wedding-card envelope, plump as if stuffed full, its flap sealed with a big round plain dark red wax seal with no marks on it, and tied with a thick crimson ribbon in a big bow. Hand-sculpted matte modeling clay, stop-motion claymation style, chunky rounded forms. One single closed object, no base, no text, no logos.

files.model.fbx: Rodin's base_basic_pbr.fbx; its embedded diffuse map is the final one, and its normal, roughness and metallic maps are flat 1-pixel images (flat normal, roughness 0.85, not metallic), so the clay stays matte

credits: Rodin reports no cost per call; about 0.5 credit a generation (T81's measurement). T105's total is in Docs/tasks/T105.md.
note: Take 1 is kept (take 2 kept the seal mark and lost the clean shape). The stamped mark was relief in the mesh and paint in the texture: fbxedit.py smoothed the seal's front vertices (171 vertices, 40 Laplacian passes) and fixtex.swift filled the seal disc in the diffuse map with its rim's median color. My person chose this.
